newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER IN LIQUID MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES SOFTER IN LIQUID MARKET.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted softer on the back of liquidity on Monday, with dealers expecting more cash inflows during the week from maturing treasury bills.

"We're expecting a liquid market with Z$500 million treasury bills maturing this week and next week we're expecting Z$1.8 billion," one dealer said, adding, however, that trade on Monday had so far been quiet.
He said discount houses were selling treasury bills at 17.50 from last Friday's 17.65 percent while call money money slid to 17.50 percent from 18.50 percent.

NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were trading at 18.75 and 18.50 percent (buying and selling respectively) from 19 and 18.25 percent and bankers acceptances were being bought at 17.80 percent from 18.50 and sold at 17.50 percent, down from 17.70 percent.
Reserve Bank figures indicated a market surplus of Z$39 million compared to a previous Z$17 million shortage. --Stella Mapenzauswa, Harare Newsroom: +263-4 72 52 28/9--
